summary: 1936 Plumas National Forest lookout on Mount Ingalls, dismantled and moved in 1984 to the Plumas County Fairgrounds in Quincy, where it is an interpretive display.

facts.design: 10-foot enclosed timber tower built to California Region 5 Plan BC-301

access.note: Displayed on the grounds of the Plumas County Fairgrounds in Quincy. Hours and current condition not confirmed in the sources read.

facts.agency: US Forest Service, Plumas National Forest

events.note: Lookout station on the top of Mount Ingalls near Walker Mine, with Ed Merry as lookout; earliest station named in the sources read
Register gives 1936 for the summit tower; the Quincy marker says a CCC company built it in 1935
Lookout Jim Bailey struck by fragments of a bullet that broke up on the catwalk; stayed at post until a replacement came
Station closed down and not to reopen the next year except in times of emergency (September 1976 report)
Structure dismantled and taken off the mountaintop
Moved to the Plumas County Fairgrounds in Quincy
Reconstructed at the fairgrounds; the marker credits Reserve Navy Mobile Construction Battalion 2

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The summit already had a lookout station by 1922, so the 1936 tower was not the first lookout on the mountain. The 1935 versus 1936 build date is not resolved and is left as a disagreement.

notes_for_editor: Three sources only, and they disagree on the build date: the register says 1936; the Quincy marker credits CCC Company 989 with building it in 1935; the Forest Lookouts page shows a lookout station on the mountain by 1922, so the 1936 tower may have replaced an earlier station. Not resolved. A 1995 Feather River Bulletin item, seen only as a search snippet (cdnc.ucr.edu), says the tower was removed in 1986, against 1984 in the register and the Forest Lookouts page. The CDNC page returned HTTP 403 and was not used. Worth checking if CDNC can be reached. The record's kind 'two_story' is not supported by anything read: the register describes a '10 foot enclosed timber tower', so the kind is left unchanged for an editor to check against firelookout.org. The record's elevation (1057 m) is the fairgrounds site (the register gives 3,468 ft there), not the summit's 8,372 ft. The record's 'relocated' entry had no year; 1984 is added. A Plumas National Forest Facebook post seen only as a search snippet mentions the lookout at fair weekends; it was not read. Current hours and condition are unverified. No photos added: the register photos have no URLs in the sources read.
